content.title: About
content.content: Cod liver oil is a nutritional oil extracted from the livers of cod fish. It has long been taken as a supplement in Northern Europe and elsewhere and is a natural source of omega-3 fatty acids and the fat-soluble vitamins A and D. It is sold as a liquid and in capsules, sometimes flavored to reduce its fishy taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cod liver oil has been used for centuries, traditionally to help prevent rickets in children.
Unlike most fish oils, which come from the flesh of fish, cod liver oil comes from the liver.
It provides EPA and DHA omega-3 fatty acids along with vitamin A and vitamin D.
Liquid cod liver oil has a strong fishy taste, so flavored versions and capsules are common.
Cod liver oil is a dietary supplement, so the amount of nutrients varies by product.

items.title: Source of omega-3 fatty acids
items.content: EPA and DHA support normal heart and brain function.

items.title: Provides vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D supports calcium absorption and normal bone and muscle function.

items.title: Provides vitamin A
items.content: Vitamin A supports vision, skin, and immune function.

items.title: Traditional supplement
items.content: It is often used as a way to get vitamin D and omega-3 when the diet is low in fish and sun exposure is limited.

items.title: Available in different forms
items.content: It is sold as liquid, capsules, and flavored products.

items.title: Too much vitamin A
items.content: Cod liver oil is high in vitamin A. Excess vitamin A can be harmful, especially during pregnancy, so do not combine it with other vitamin A supplements and follow your doctor's advice.

items.title: Too much vitamin D
items.content: Excess vitamin D can raise calcium levels in the blood. Follow the label and your healthcare professional's advice.

items.title: Possible medication interactions
items.content: High doses of omega-3 and vitamin A or D may interact with medications such as blood thinners. People taking prescription drugs should consult a healthcare professional.

items.title: Side effects and allergies
items.content: Cod liver oil may cause fishy burps, heartburn, or nausea. It should be avoided by people allergic to fish.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cod liver oil is taken as a liquid or in capsules, usually with a meal to reduce stomach upset. Follow the dose on the label or the advice of a healthcare professional, and ask a doctor or pharmacist before giving it to children. Flavored liquids or capsules can help with the taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cod liver oil in a tightly closed bottle in a cool, dark place, and refrigerate it after opening if the label says so. Keep it away from heat and light. Check the expiration date and discard oil that smells rancid.
